To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dye 1.9-dimethylmethylenblue (DMM) binds to teichoic acid (S. aureus TA) with 1: 1 stoichiometry, and that the TA-DMMB complex is a helical confoimation, as evidenced by the strong CD induced by the complex in the DMMB dye.
the dye 1.9-dimethyl-methyleneblue is a useful tool for studying the structure of teichoic acids.

the dye DMMB binds with 1: 1 stoichiometry to the wall teichoic acids (TA) of the Gram-positive bacterium Staphylocococcus aureus, and that this binding induces metachromasia as well as strong circular dichroic spectra.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of a dye, 1,9-Dimethyl methylene Blue, with a teichoic acid from the Gram-positive bacterium, Staphylococci aureus.
the study of interactions of TA with a series of cationic dyes.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of the induction of metachromasy by the bacterial cell surface component TA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metachromasia of DMMB is not a property of TA alone, but is induced by the TA in the presence of DMMB.
the TA-DMMB complex is a helical structure.
TA in dilution at neutral pH has the conformation of a random coil polymer and not of a helix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S. aureus cell wall TA has a conformation which is intermediate in nature between the random coil and helical conformations of DNA.
TA in dilution at neutral pH has helical conformation.
TA has a helical secondary structure, which is not a random coiled polymer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metachromasia induced by the S. aureus teichoic acid in DMMB is a consequence of the binding of the dye to the helical structure of TA.
the metachromasia of DMMB by TA is a useful method for the detection of TA in bacterial cell walls.
TA is a polyanion and it can induce metachromasia as well as CD in a cationic dye like DMMB, and that the dye is sensitive enough to detect the helical conformation of the polymer.
